about.title: South Pasadena Product Liability Claims
about.longDescription: South Pasadena is a small, walkable city, but defective products still cause serious harm here — a malfunctioning appliance in a Fremont Avenue bungalow, a faulty car part on Fair Oaks Avenue, or a broken tool used near Huntington Drive. California treats these cases differently than most personal injury matters: because product claims often rely on strict liability, an injured person generally doesn't have to prove the manufacturer was careless, only that the product was defective and caused harm. That distinction matters, because it can open the door to claims against manufacturers, distributors, and retailers alike. If a product failed you or a family member in South Pasadena, keeping the item itself and any packaging can matter more than you'd expect. LawProactive doesn't practice law — we simply connect you, free of charge, with an independent attorney who can look at what happened and explain your options, without any obligation on your part.

whyChoose.title: Why This Matters Under California Law

items.title: Strict Liability Can Simplify the Burden
items.desc: You generally don't need to prove the manufacturer was negligent — only that the product was defective and caused your injury. This can make certain claims more direct than typical negligence cases.

items.title: Multiple Parties May Share Responsibility
items.desc: Manufacturers, distributors, and retailers can all potentially be held liable for a defective product. An attorney can help identify which parties were involved in getting the product to you.

items.title: The Product Itself Is Evidence
items.desc: Because defect claims often hinge on design, manufacturing, or warning flaws, preserving the actual item — not just photos — can matter significantly to how a claim is evaluated.

items.question: Do I need to prove the manufacturer was careless?
items.answer: Not necessarily. California's strict liability approach to defective products generally focuses on whether the product itself was unreasonably dangerous, not on the manufacturer's state of mind. An attorney can review your situation to see which theory fits best.

items.question: I still have the broken product from an incident near Fair Oaks Avenue — does that matter?
items.answer: Yes, keeping the product, its packaging, and any manuals can be important. Physical evidence often plays a central role in showing whether a defect existed. Try to store it safely and avoid further alterations or repairs.

items.question: Is there a cost to talk with an attorney through LawProactive?
items.answer: No. LawProactive is a free service that connects you with an independent attorney in our network, and attorneys who take these cases typically work on contingency, meaning no fee unless there's a recovery. There's no obligation to move forward after speaking with someone.

items.question: What if the defective product was bought outside South Pasadena but the injury happened here?
items.answer: That's common and generally doesn't prevent a claim. What matters more is where the injury occurred and who was involved in manufacturing, distributing, or selling the product. An attorney can help sort out the details specific to your case.
